question: A _______ bit is an extra bit included with a binary message to make the total number of 1's either odd or even.
solution:
The correct answer is __**parity**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A parity bit is an extra bit included with a binary message to make the total number of 1s either odd or even.
 
• Parity bits are used in error detection schemes to ensure data integrity during transmission.
 
• There are two types of parity: **even parity** and **odd parity**.
 
• In even parity, the parity bit is set so that the total number of 1s in the message is even.
 
• In odd parity, the parity bit is set so that the total number of 1s in the message is odd.
 
• Parity bits are a simple and commonly used method for detecting errors in data transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Parity bits are not used for error correction, only for error detection.
 
• If an error is detected using a parity bit, other methods must be employed to correct the error.
 
• More advanced error detection and correction techniques include checksums, cyclic redundancy checks (CRC), and Hamming codes.
 
• Parity bits are often used in conjunction with other error detection and correction methods to provide robust data integrity.

subject: COMPUTER
question: What does QR in 'QR code' stand for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Quick Response**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• QR code stands for **Quick Response** code.
 
• It was invented in **1994** by the Japanese company **Denso Wave**.
 
• The QR code system was originally designed to track parts in vehicle manufacturing.
 
• QR codes are two-dimensional barcodes that can store a significant amount of information compared to traditional barcodes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Barcode vs. QR Code**

 
 
• **Barcode:** A barcode is a machine-readable optical label that contains information about the item to which it is attached. Barcodes are typically one-dimensional and can hold up to 20 characters.
 
• **QR Code:** A QR code is a type of two-dimensional barcode that can contain more data than a traditional barcode. It can hold up to 7,089 numeric characters or 4,296 alphanumeric characters.
 
 
 
• **Applications of QR Codes**
 
 
• **Product Tracking:** QR codes are used in manufacturing and logistics for tracking products and parts.
 
• **Payment Systems:** Many mobile payment systems, such as those used in China, use QR codes to facilitate transactions.
 
• **Marketing and Advertising:** QR codes are used in marketing materials to direct consumers to websites, promotions, and more.
 
• **Event Ticketing:** QR codes are often used for electronic tickets and event registration.
 
 
 
• **How to Read a QR Code**
 
 
• QR codes can be read using a QR code scanner, which is available as a feature on many smartphones and dedicated QR code reader devices.
 
• To scan a QR code, you typically open the QR code scanning app or the camera app on your smartphone and point it at the QR code until it is recognized.
 
• Once scanned, the encoded information will be displayed or the appropriate action (such as opening a website) will be taken.

question: What is the role of ROM (Read - Only Memory) in a computer system?

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a type of non-volatile memory used in computers and other electronic devices.
 
• It is primarily used to store the computer's **firmware and startup instructions**.
 
• Firmware is a specific class of computer software that provides the low-level control for the device's specific hardware.
 
• Unlike RAM (Random Access Memory), ROM retains its contents even when the computer is powered off.
 
• This makes ROM crucial for the **booting process** of the computer, as it holds the initial program that the processor uses to start the computer system after it is turned on.

• There are different types of ROM, including **PROM (Programmable ROM), EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM), and EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM)**.
 
• EEPROM can be reprogrammed and erased multiple times using an electrical charge, making it more flexible than other types of ROM.
 
• ROM is essential for the basic functioning of any computer system, ensuring that critical software is always available to the hardware.

• **Black hat hackers**, also known as **crackers**, are individuals who engage in **unethical and illegal activities**.
 
• They hack to gain **unauthorized access **to a system with the intent of **causing damage, stealing sensitive information, or disrupting its operations**.
 
• Black hat hackers often have a **deep understanding of computer networks and systems.**
 
• Their activities are not only limited to gaining unauthorized access but also **manipulating the data and system configurations.**
 
• Black hat hacking can result in** substantial harm to individuals, organizations, and the public, and it is illegal and punishable by law**.

• **White hat**

• They are usually employed by organizations to conduct penetration tests and vulnerability assessments on the companies' systems to prevent potential breaches.
 
 
 
• **Red hat**
 
 
• Red hat hackers are similar to white hat hackers in that their intent is to prevent malicious hacking.
 
• However, instead of simply aiming to defend systems or fix vulnerabilities, they actively engage with black hat hackers, even attacking their systems to bring them down.
 
• This proactive (and at times aggressive) approach separates them from white hat hackers.
 
 
 
• **Grey hat**
 
 
• Grey hat hackers operate in the gray area between malicious intent (black hat) and ethical hacking (white hat).
 
• While they may not have permission to access systems like white hat hackers do, they typically alert organizations to vulnerabilities they find, giving them a chance to fix the issues before less ethical hackers can exploit them.
 
• However, some gray hat hackers may also request a fee for fixing such vulnerabilities.

question: In Windows OS, when you delete an item from any of the drives by making use of the ‘Delete’ key or even by simply right-clicking and selecting the ‘Delete’ option, the item is moved to ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Recycle Bin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a special folder in Windows that **temporarily stores deleted files and folders.**
 
• When you delete an item, it is moved to the Recycle Bin rather than permanently deleted.
 
• To delete a file using File Explorer, you need to locate the file and **either press your Delete key or click Delete on the Home tab of the ribbon.** You can even **select more than one file** to delete at the same time.
 
• From the Recycle Bin, **items can be restored to their original locations** if you realize you've made a mistake or need the files/folders again. However, files bypass the Recycle Bin if they're too large or if you've specifically directed Windows to delete them permanently.
 
• The Recycle Bin is per drive, meaning each drive in your system has its own dedicated Recycle Bin. For example, if you delete a file from Drive C, it goes to the Recycle Bin of Drive C.
 
• The Recycle Bin is automatically created and managed by Windows, and **users can adjust the disk space allocated to the Recycle Bin** by right-clicking on the Recycle Bin icon and choosing "Properties".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Control Panel:**

 
 
• The Control Panel is a component of Microsoft Windows that provides the ability to view and adjust system settings and controls, such as adding hardware, adding and removing software, controlling user accounts, and changing accessibility options.
 
• From Windows 95 to Windows XP, the Control Panel is a standard interface; however, since Windows 8, a simplified Control Panel called "Settings" has been introduced and is being continually enhanced in more recent versions.
 
 
 
• **Taskbar:**
 
 
• The Taskbar refers to the application bar which is by default set to the bottom of the screen in Windows operating systems.
 
• It includes the 'Start' button, the Cortana search box (in later versions), application shortcuts, and system icons, among others.
 
• The taskbar allows users to view the current status of their open applications as well as launch new ones; it also contains the system clock and notification area.
 
• The Taskbar properties allow customization like altering its location on the screen, changing its size, and determining how taskbar buttons group together.
 
 
 
• **Start menu:**
 
 
• The Start menu is a user interface element in Microsoft Windows, providing a central launching point for applications and tasks.
 
• It offers quick access to programs and system settings, documents, and files.
 
• It also contains links to network connections, printers, and your computer, as well as recent documents and help and support.
 
• The function of the Start menu has evolved since its inception in Windows 95; in Windows 10, it includes Live Tiles to the right of the menu.

question: What does the Ctrl + V shortcut key do?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pastes the copied content**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Ctrl + V shortcut key is used to paste content that has been copied or cut to the clipboard.

• This function is available in most applications, including word processors, web browsers, and other software that supports text editing.

• When you press Ctrl + V, the content from the clipboard is inserted at the current cursor position.

• This shortcut is part of the standard set of keyboard shortcuts for copy, cut, and paste operations, which includes Ctrl + C (copy) and Ctrl + X (cut).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Clipboard**

• The clipboard is a temporary storage area in the computer's memory where data that is cut or copied is stored.

• The clipboard can hold text, images, files, and other types of data.

• The contents of the clipboard remain available until they are replaced by new data or until the computer is shut down.

• **Copy (Ctrl + C)**

• This shortcut key is used to copy the selected content to the clipboard without removing it from its original location.

• After copying, the content can be pasted elsewhere using the Ctrl + V shortcut.

• **Cut (Ctrl + X)**

• This shortcut key is used to cut the selected content, removing it from its original location and placing it in the clipboard.

• The cut content can then be pasted to a new location using the Ctrl + V shortcut.

• **Paste (Ctrl + V)**

• This shortcut key is used to paste the content from the clipboard to the current cursor position or selected location.

• Pasting does not remove the content from the clipboard, allowing it to be pasted multiple times.

</ul
